svg.title: The Buy-Instead-of-Build Process
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-eta-buy-side-process; chapter number: 1; title: The Buy-Instead-of-Build Process; subtitle: From belly-to-belly sourcing to a six-month change freeze; chart type: process_flow; stages: step: 01; label: Source Belly to Belly; value: Step 1; detail: Work brokers, trade-show lists and direct outreach in one geography; Ruback says belly-to-belly sales beat national email campaigns, and a Houston searcher never had lunch alone.; step: 02; label: Screen Near 4x Cash Flow; value: Step 2; detail: Screen at about 4x cash flow and stay away from anything too asset or capital intensive (Chicago Booth); map revenue by referral source.; step: 03; label: Open at 2.5x, Concede Up to Half a Turn; value: Step 3; detail: Searcher Antonio opens at 2.5x; Ruback gives a quarter or half turn to preserve goodwill, because if the deal is good at 3, it is still good.; step: 04; label: LOI, 60-Day Diligence, QoE; value: Step 4; detail: Close on an LOI, 60 days of diligence and a QoE; reconcile 36 months of bank statements and kill or reprice any target with two sets of books.; step: 05; label: Fund, Then Freeze for Six Months; value: Step 5; detail: Fund with SBA 7(a) debt up to $5M, a seller note and $100-150K of working capital; freeze personnel changes for six months post-close.; caption: The street mechanics of entrepreneurship through acquisition, from sourcing and screening through price, diligence, funding and the post-close freeze.; assumptions note: Every multiple, dollar figure and time window is quoted from Q1 practitioners; the 4x screen and 2.5x opening offer are practitioner rules, not market averages.; note: Attributed to HBS Rock Center for Entrepreneurship (oJcm3Bn-lXE at 00:46:43 and 00:57:40), The University of Chicago Booth School of Business (60ZOJolZwOo), Technically News (nOnsMlkLh10 at 00:58:06 and 01:08:24) and The Wall Street Skinny (MpeYmBDptXs at 00:44:27).

rect.title: step: 01; label: Source Belly to Belly; value: Step 1; detail: Work brokers, trade-show lists and direct outreach in one geography; Ruback says belly-to-belly sales beat national email campaigns, and a Houston searcher never had lunch alone.
